findings.title: PCPJack | Cloud Worm Evicts TeamPCP and Steals Credentials at Scale
findings.summary_md: SentinelLABS identified PCPJack, a credential theft framework that worms across exposed cloud infrastructure and removes artifacts associated with TeamPCP, a threat actor persona behind several high-profile supply chain intrusions in early 2026. The toolset harvests credentials from cloud, container, developer, productivity, and financial services, then exfiltrates data through attacker-controlled infrastructure while spreading to additional hosts. PCPJack targets exposed services including Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, MongoDB, RayML, and vulnerable web applications, and does not deploy cryptominers. SentinelLABS located the first script on 28 April 2026 through a Kubernetes-focused VirusTotal hunting rule.

findings.title: PCPJack Credential Stealer Exploits 5 CVEs to Spread Worm-Like Across Cloud Systems
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported on SentinelOne researcher Alex Delamotte's analysis of PCPJack, a credential theft framework that targets exposed cloud infrastructure and removes TeamPCP artifacts. PCPJack targets Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, MongoDB, RayML, and vulnerable web applications, spreading worm-like and moving laterally inside compromised networks. Its assessed end goal is illicit revenue through credential theft, fraud, spam, extortion, or resale of stolen access, and it notably lacks a cryptomining component. The report notes targeting overlaps with TeamPCP, which rose to prominence by exploiting vulnerabilities such as React2Shell and cloud misconfigurations.

findings.title: Hackers hack victims hacked by other hackers
findings.summary_md: TechCrunch reported that an unknown group targeted systems already compromised by TeamPCP, kicking out TeamPCP and removing its tools before deploying worm-spreading code to steal credentials across cloud infrastructure. Alex Delamotte of SentinelOne, who found and named PCPJack, told TechCrunch it is unclear who is behind the campaign. TeamPCP had recently drawn attention through high-profile supply chain hacks, including a breach of the European Commission. The report describes PCPJack as replicating across cloud infrastructure and exfiltrating stolen credentials to attacker-controlled systems.
